layer2.details: Layer 2 effect observed via kubectl_verify: target cart pod CPU was very high on 3 observations (6259m, 6432m, 6401m). Namespace-wide top showed other otel-demo pods mostly 0–23m CPU, supporting target-specific CPU-load effect; target pod remained Running/Ready with 0 restarts.

warnings: Baseline data was explicitly reported as unavailable/unusable, so verification relies on repeated absolute CPU observations plus current cross-resource comparison rather than pre-injection delta.

Negative Evidence: (1) kubectl_verify exec was unavailable/rejected, so chaos CPU process could not be directly listed; accepted as a limitation, not a contradiction of CPU metric evidence. (2) kubectl_verify logs did not show timeout/slow-request errors; accepted as valid counter-evidence that application-level degradation was not observed in sampled logs. (3) target pod remained Ready/Running with 0 restarts; this weakens any claim of severe failure but is compatible with CPU-load injection. (4) kubectl get events with field-selector was rejected by the proxy; event evidence is unavailable. (5) Baseline unavailable means exact percentage increase from pre-injection cannot be computed.
Polling requirement satisfied: CPU was checked at least 3 times by kubectl_verify and remained high (6259m → 6432m → 6401m).

Recovery was not verified in this Layer 2 active-fault check because the experiment is still active per Layer 1 context and verifier tools cannot destroy the experiment; recovery must be assessed after destroy or timeout.

Checklist-conclusion inconsistency: Step(s) [2, 3] marked 'failed' but Layer2 concluded 'passed'. The LLM may have determined these failures are benign (e.g., timing delays). Overall field is the final authority.

items.evidence: CPU usage monitoring: baseline unavailable → current observed by kubectl_verify top pod cart-7c58f6bb56-zdp5w = 6259m, later 6401m; namespace top also showed cart = 6432m while other otel-demo pods were mostly 0–23m. This is strong primary evidence of pod-cpu fullload effect.

Process confirmation inside container: baseline unavailable → current kubectl_verify exec cart-7c58f6bb56-zdp5w -- ps aux could not be executed because verifier proxy rejected exec except controlled blade commands. No process list evidence was obtainable by this method.

Application log / latency symptom check: baseline unavailable → current kubectl_verify logs showed normal cart operations (GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync/EmptyCartAsync) and did not show timeout, slow request, or high-latency messages in the sampled tail. Application-level degradation was not confirmed from logs.

Coverage check: baseline unavailable → current kubectl_verify get pods -n otel-demo -l app.kubernetes.io/name=cart showed exactly one current cart pod, cart-7c58f6bb56-zdp5w; current top observations showed this same pod at ~6.3–6.4 cores, so all discovered target cart pods were covered.

Anomaly / non-target comparison: baseline unavailable → current kubectl_verify top pod -n otel-demo showed non-target pods low relative to cart (examples: accounting 1m, frontend 10m, otel-collector 23m, load-generator 14m) while cart was 6432m; no unexpected comparable CPU spike on non-target resources was observed.

Pod health state: baseline unavailable → current kubectl_verify get pod cart-7c58f6bb56-zdp5w -n otel-demo -o wide showed READY=1/1, STATUS=Running, RESTARTS=0. Fault did not kill or restart the target pod during observation.
